newsitem.title: USA: US tax conferees still at odds on muni matters.
newsitem.headline: US tax conferees still at odds on muni matters.

text.p: U.S. senators negotiating the tax bill on Thursday refused to cave in to the House on a number of provisions affecting tax-exempt bonds, a Senate document shows.
In their first counteroffer to the House on the massive tax bill, Senate conferees refused to scale back their chamber's proposed repeal of the $150 million volume cap on 501(c)(3) bonds.
The House had voted earlier to increase the volume cap by $50 million over five years to a total $200 million. The Senate, however, had voted to repeal the cap altogether.
Senators also refused to drop a provision that would increase from $5 million to $10 million the arbitrage rebate exception for small issuers of public school infrastructure bonds.
And they said they are sticking with a proposal to hike from $10 million to $20 million the ceiling on capital expenditures by firms issuing small-issue industrial development bonds.
In one concession, the Senate accepted a House proposal to allow refunding of certain tax-exempt Virgin Island bonds.

Senators also accepted a compromise proposed by House conferees regarding issuance of mortgage revenue bonds in disaster areas. Under the compromise, mortgage revenue bond requirements would be loosened in Presidentially declared disaster areas for two years.
House and Senate conferees so far have not worked out differences provisions designed to assist the financially struggling District of Columbia.
